squeeze.note: composite of short_float+ctb over the inputs present (see components); FINRA daily short-sale volume is intentionally excluded because it is non-directional, and days-to-cover/short_ratio is not exposed on this fast path

components.name: bearish_analyst
components.definition: a reliable author's NEWEST call on the symbol is short/reduce and dated in the last 28 days
components.source: Seeking Alpha contributors passing the reliability gate (GetAnalystTradeIdeas)
components.history: about 13 months of article history; reliability is scored on the same history, so only the point-in-time rebuild in the event study is out-of-sample

components.name: sell_side_downgrades
components.definition: >= 2 downgrades by distinct firms dated in the last 28 days
components.history: about 2 years of dated actions per symbol (Finviz); the event study used a 6-year Yahoo crawl

components.name: insider_selling
components.definition: >= 2 distinct insiders sold on the open market for >= $1000000 in total, and no open-market purchase, in filings public in the last 30 days
components.source: SEC EDGAR Form 4 (local corpus; official filings only)
components.history: corpus history is only partly certified (13 of 5820 index days at the time of writing), so live reads are coverage-gated; the event study used SEC's public Form 345 datasets (2020-2026) instead

components.name: technical_damage
components.definition: close below SMA200 AND 12-1 month momentum < 0 AND 63-session return below SPY's
components.history: years of daily bars (point in time by construction)

components.name: bearish_put_call
components.definition: put/call volume ratio > 1.5 (the risk detector's threshold)
components.detail: no value available for this symbol
components.history: none: only today's chain is read; no stored history
components.unmeasured_reason: current snapshot only, no point-in-time history to test

components.name: high_short_float
components.definition: short float >= 20% of float (descriptive level, not fitted; can also mean squeeze risk)
components.source: static data short float, current snapshot
components.history: none: the daily snapshot store does not record short interest
components.unmeasured_reason: current snapshot only, no point-in-time history to test

components.name: high_cost_to_borrow
components.definition: cost to borrow > 30% (the risk detector's threshold)
components.history: none: only the current rate is read
components.unmeasured_reason: current snapshot only, no point-in-time history to test

components.name: consensus_deterioration
components.definition: consensus rating score (5 strong buy .. 1 strong sell) fell by >= 0.2 over the recorded span
components.source: StockAnalysis consensus via the daily snapshot store
components.history: forward-only: recording started with the snapshot worker (about 5 weeks at the time of writing)
components.unmeasured_reason: too short a history for an event study

validations.caveat: the classic loser/momentum drift, not evidence about any other component; negative in every calendar year 2021-2026 but far from uniform (-1.4% to -6.5%); no effect at 21 sessions that passes the rule; current-listing universe only, so delisted losers are missing and the true drift is likely larger

bearish_dossier.note: Counts of components with evidence, not a score and not a forecast. status='unvalidated' means no out-of-sample test supports this combination; unmeasured components are context (current snapshots, no history). See rules.bearish_dossier in the tool description for the measured results.

bearish_dossier.cannot_control: Survivorship: only current listings have prices, delisted names are absent. Liquidity and sector/market cap use today's values (market cap is rebuilt point in time from price). Overlapping windows (weekly signals, 21/63-session horizons) are handled only by clustering. Matching does not control beta, volatility or momentum; a component that proxies momentum will show it. Equal-weighted, before costs, no shorting frictions (borrow, squeeze) which matter most for the names this view flags. Technical damage uses dividend-adjusted closes in the study and daily bar closes in the live view. The sell-side study used a Yahoo history, the live view Finviz; the insider study used SEC's public Form 4 data sets (2020-2026-03), not the local corpus, whose history is only partly certified.
bearish_dossier.inventory: bearish_analyst: about 13 months of article history, point-in-time reliability rebuilt (measurable, thin); sell_side_downgrades: Yahoo history ~6 years, Finviz ~2 years (measurable); insider_selling: SEC data sets 2020-2026-03 (measurable); the local SEC corpus is certified for only a handful of days, so live insider reads are unknown unless a cluster is actually observed; technical_damage: years of bars (measurable); bearish_put_call, high_short_float, high_cost_to_borrow: current snapshots only (unmeasured); consensus_deterioration: forward-only since the snapshot worker started, about 5 weeks (unmeasured)
bearish_dossier.measured_flag: measured=true means a point-in-time history exists that an event study can use; measured=false components are current snapshots only (put/call, short float, cost to borrow) or forward-only history of about 5 weeks (consensus), shown as context and counted in active_unmeasured.
bearish_dossier.purpose: One place for the bearish evidence we hold on a symbol. It lists components with state active/inactive/unknown, the evidence, and counts. There is NO score and NO forecast: active_count is a plain count of active components.
bearish_dossier.result: Validated: technical_damage at 63 sessions only (mean matched excess -2.83%, 95% CI [-3.96%, -1.68%], n=169,599 over 3,120 tickers; first half -1.85%, second half -3.92% with CI [-5.71%, -2.24%]; underperforms by more than 1% in 54.2% of cases vs 49.7% for controls). It is the known loser/momentum drift: it says nothing about analysts, insiders or sell-side. NOT validated: sell_side_downgrades (matched excess +0.25% at 21 and +0.79% at 63 sessions: no underperformance), insider_selling (matched excess +0.41% at 21 and +1.09% at 63 sessions: stocks with insider selling clusters did NOT underperform), bearish_analyst (245 events from at most 4 point-in-time reliable authors, all in 2025-26; 21-session matched excess -1.7%, CI [-4.0%, +0.5%]; 63 sessions +2.7%, n=95: too little history to say), count 2 (63-session matched excess -2.35%, but -0.69% in the first half with a CI spanning zero, and the extra components add nothing over technical_damage alone: technical_damage alone -3.01%, with insider_selling -3.53%, with sell_side_downgrades -0.43%), count 3+ (147 observations, no result).
bearish_dossier.states: active = condition met on data we could read; inactive = we read the data and the condition is not met; unknown = the data could not be read or coverage is not certified (never shown as inactive).
bearish_dossier.status: 'unvalidated' by default. 'measured' only when an ACTIVE component is listed in validations, i.e. it passed the out-of-sample rule below. Any other combination, including 2 or more components, stays 'unvalidated'.
bearish_dossier.study: Event study, signals sampled every 5 sessions from 2021-10 to 2026-08 on about 3,600 US stocks (liquid today, price >= $5). Forward 21- and 63-session returns from the signal close; excess vs SPY and vs a matched control (same date, same sector and point-in-time market-cap tercile, without the component). Cluster bootstrap 95% intervals (ticker x month, month, ticker; the widest is used). Halves split at 2024-01-03. Rule fixed beforehand: a component or a count>=2 bucket is a candidate if its first-half matched excess is negative with a 95% interval below zero; it is validated only if its second-half interval, at the Bonferroni level over the candidates, is below zero, with at least 100 observations and 30 clusters, the short-hit rate above the control's, and no sign reversal between halves.
bearish_dossier.verdict: No combination of components beats matched controls out of sample. The only measured effect is the technical damage component on its own; the analyst, sell-side and insider components should be read as context, not as evidence that the stock will fall.
